settings.heading: The Health Benefits of Honey
settings.text: Discover why honey has been treasured for thousands of years. From its naturally occurring antioxidants to its versatility in everyday recipes, learn how premium honey can be enjoyed as part of a healthy, balanced lifestyle.

Nature's Original Sweetener

Honey has been enjoyed around the world for thousands of years. Unlike refined sugar, honey is produced naturally by honeybees using nectar collected from flowering plants. Every jar reflects the flowers visited by the bees, giving each variety its own unique flavour, colour and aroma.

Premium honey also contains naturally occurring plant compounds, trace minerals, enzymes and antioxidants that contribute to its distinctive character. The exact composition varies depending on the flowers the bees visit, making every honey variety wonderfully unique.

Whether stirred into tea, drizzled over yoghurt or used in savoury cooking, honey offers a naturally sweet alternative that brings far more than sweetness alone.

settings.heading: Naturally Occurring Antioxidants
settings.text: A Natural Source of Plant Compounds Honey naturally contains antioxidants, including plant compounds known as polyphenols and flavonoids. These compounds occur naturally in many fruits, vegetables, herbs and flowers and contribute to the unique colour and flavour of different honey varieties. Generally speaking, darker honeys tend to contain higher levels of antioxidants, although every floral source is different. The nectar collected by bees directly influences the character of the finished honey, meaning every BeeBlend variety offers its own distinctive taste profile.

Its smooth texture and rich flavour also make it an excellent ingredient in homemade energy bites and granola.

settings.q: What makes honey different from refined sugar?
settings.a: Honey is produced by honeybees from flower nectar, and its flavour, colour and aroma vary according to its floral source. This gives different honey varieties their own distinctive character. Like all sweeteners, honey is best enjoyed in moderation as part of a balanced diet.

settings.q: Can I enjoy honey every day?
settings.a: Yes, many people enjoy honey every day in breakfasts, hot drinks, smoothies and cooking. Like all sweeteners, it's best enjoyed as part of a varied and balanced diet.
Yes. Honey naturally contains antioxidants, including plant compounds such as polyphenols and flavonoids. The exact levels vary depending on the flowers visited by the bees.
Crystallisation is a completely natural process that can occur in honey. Simply stand the jar in warm water and stir gently if you prefer a smoother consistency.

settings.q: Does crystallised honey mean it has gone bad?
settings.a: Not at all. Crystallisation is a natural characteristic of real honey and does not affect its quality or safety.
Store your honey in a cool, dry place with the lid tightly sealed. There's no need to refrigerate it, as this can encourage crystallisation.

Honey has an exceptionally long shelf life when stored correctly. While its flavour, colour and texture may naturally change over time, it remains enjoyable for a long time when kept sealed in suitable conditions.

settings.q: Can I cook and bake with honey?
settings.a: Absolutely. Honey is a versatile ingredient that's perfect for marinades, glazes, dressings, baking, desserts and hot drinks.

settings.a: If you enjoy lighter flavours, try Lychee Honey or Kashmiri Acacia Honey. For cooking, Yellow Mustard Honey and Wild Fennel Honey are excellent choices. If you're looking for something indulgent, Golden Nut Honey is perfect for breakfasts, desserts and cheese boards.

settings.q: Why do different honeys taste different?
settings.a: The flavour, colour and aroma of honey depend on the flowers visited by the bees. Different floral sources create unique honey varieties, each with its own distinctive characteristics.
Honey should not be given to babies under 12 months of age. Older children and adults can enjoy honey as part of a balanced diet.
